Just weeks after announcing a price hike for Apple Music, Apple has now revealed that Apple TV will also see a price increase. Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that the monthly fee for Apple TV will rise from US$12.99 to US$14.99.

The monthly fee for the Apple One Individual plan will also be adjusted upward.

Apple TV and Apple One both see price hikes

Here are the details of the price increases:

  • Apple TV (monthly): US$14.99 (previously US$12.99)
  • Apple TV (annual): US$119 (previously US$99)
  • Apple One Individual: US$21.95 (previously US$19.95)

Other Apple One plan prices remain unchanged. When Apple raised the price of Apple Music last month, it also increased the Apple One Family and Apple One Premier plans at the same time, but did not adjust the Individual plan.

New subscribers will be charged at the new price starting today. Apple says existing subscribers will receive a notice of the price increase approximately one month in advance.

The last time Apple raised the monthly fee for Apple TV was in August 2025, when it went from US$12.99 to US$9.99. At that time, Apple did not adjust the annual plan or Apple One bundle pricing.

Over the past year, Apple has significantly expanded the content lineup on Apple TV. Last October, Apple announced it had become the exclusive broadcast partner for Formula 1 (F1) in the United States. The F1 streaming service is included in the standard Apple TV monthly fee at no extra charge.

Earlier this year, Apple also added Major League Soccer (MLS) match streaming to Apple TV, again at no additional cost. Previously, watching MLS required a separate subscription to MLS Season Pass.

Apple has also performed strongly thanks to the recent popularity of several titles, including the fourth season of Ted Lasso. Apple TV premiered the second season of Dark Matter this week, while the sixth season of Slow Horses will begin airing on September 16.

What do you think of Apple TV's new pricing? Is US$14.99 good value? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
